zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Quraysh
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾ ("for the accustoming of Quraysh"): there are three ways [of saying] it: ”لِإلافِ قُرَيْشٍ“, ﴿لإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾, and a third way, ”لِإلْفِ قُرَيْشٍ“. It has been read in the first two ways.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying: ﴿إيلافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ والصَّيْفِ﴾ ("their accustoming to the journey of winter and summer"): what was permissible in ”لِإيلافِ“ is permissible in it, except that in this one it has been read ”إلْفِهِمْ“ and ”إيلافِهِمْ“, and ”إلافِهِمْ“ is permissible.
Regarding this lām, the grammarians gave three views. It was said: it is connected with what precedes it; the meaning is: "He made them like eaten-up straw for the accustoming of Quraysh", that is, Allah destroyed the people of the elephant so that Quraysh might remain, together with what they had become accustomed to of the journey of winter and summer. Some said: this is the lām of wonder (lām al-taʿajjub), so the meaning would be: "Wonder at the accustoming of Quraysh!" And the grammarians whose Arabic is approved said: this lām's sense is connected with what follows, ”فَلْيَعْبُدُوا“; the meaning is: "So let these worship the Lord of this House because of their accustoming to the journey of winter and summer."
The interpretation is that Quraysh used to travel in winter to Syria and in summer to Yemen and bring back provisions; they were safe on the two journeys while people [around them] were being snatched away. When anyone accosted them, they would say: "We are the people of Allah's Sanctuary", and they would not be molested. So Allah, Glorified is He, made known that what He did for these people is among the proofs of His oneness, because they were in a land without crops and yet they were safe in it. Allah, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أنّا جَعَلْنا حَرَمًا آمِنًا ويُتَخَطَّفُ النّاسُ مِن حَوْلِهِمْ أفَبِالباطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ وبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 67] ("have they not seen that We made a secure Sanctuary while people are snatched away all around them? Do they then believe in falsehood and disbelieve in the favour of Allah?"), that is: they believe in the idols and disbelieve in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, Who bestowed this favour upon them. So He commanded them to worship Him alone, because He had accustomed them to these two journeys.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿أطْعَمَهم مِن جُوعٍ﴾ ("Who fed them against hunger"): they had been afflicted by hardship until they ate carrion and carcasses. ﴿وَآمَنَهم مِن خَوْفٍ﴾ ("and made them safe from fear"): He made them safe from fearing in the Sanctuary and from fearing on their journey. One says ”ألِفْتُ المَكانَ، آلَفُهُ، إلْفًا“ ("I became accustomed to the place"), and ”آلَفْتُ المَكانَ“ in the sense of ”ألِفْتُ“, [with the forms] ”أوْلِفُهُ، إيلافًا“. [Translator's note: so in the source; the expected imperfect of «آلَفْتُ» is «أُولِفُهُ».]
